definition_zh: 高血压（症）；血压过高；局部循环高压；过度紧张
definition_en: a condition in which blood pressure stays abnormally high, or a state of excessive tension
core_image: 一根被从里面撑紧的血管，压力表指针顶到红区
scene: 中年人体检时两次读数都偏高，医生让他先改善饮食。The nurse explained that his hypertension was mild and could be managed with diet.
sceneCN: 这里 hypertension 是「高血压」（第 1 个义项：血压长期高于正常范围的疾病）；句意为护士说明他的高血压属于轻度，可以通过饮食控制。

collocations.zh: 白大衣高血压（诊室紧张导致的暂时升高）

derivatives.zh: 高血压的；也作名词指高血压患者
抗高血压的；也作名词指降压药
低血压，把 hyper- 换成 hypo- 构成的反义词

senses.title: Persistently high blood pressure
senses.definition: a long-term condition in which the pressure of blood against the artery walls stays above the normal range
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁的压力长期高于正常范围的慢性病
senses.example: Hypertension often causes no symptoms until the heart or the kidneys are damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 高血压常常没有症状，直到心脏或肾脏受损才被发现。
senses.why: The Greek prefix hyper- means over, and tension is a stretching, so the word pictures an artery stretched tighter than it should be.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 hyper- 表示「超过」，tension 是「拉紧」，所以这个词描绘的是血管被绷得比应有的更紧。

senses.title: A reading above the line
senses.definition: a blood-pressure measurement that is above the normal range, especially one taken on a single visit
senses.definitionCN: 高于正常范围的血压测量值，尤指单次就诊时的读数
senses.example: Her home monitor showed hypertension on three mornings in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家用血压计连续三个早晨都显示血压偏高。
senses.why: Because the disease is defined by a number, the same word also names the high reading that first reveals it.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种病是靠数值来定义的，所以同一个词也用来指第一次暴露它的那个偏高读数。

senses.title: High pressure in one vessel bed
senses.definition: abnormally high pressure inside one section of the circulation, as in pulmonary or portal hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 某一局部循环内的压力异常升高，如肺动脉高压或门静脉高压
senses.example: Pulmonary hypertension makes the right side of the heart work much harder.
senses.exampleCN: 肺动脉高压使右心室负担加重许多。
senses.why: The core image can be narrowed to a single vessel bed, so clinicians speak of high pressure in the lungs or in the liver.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象可以缩小到某一处血管床，所以临床上会说肺里或肝里的局部高压。

senses.title: Nerves pulled too tight
senses.definition: a state of great or excessive psychological tension in a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体过度紧张、绷得太紧的精神状态
senses.example: Months of waiting left the whole family in a state of hypertension.
senses.exampleCN: 数月的等待让全家人都处在一种过度紧张的状态里。
senses.why: The medical image of a vessel stretched too tight transfers easily to nerves stretched too tight.
senses.whyCN: 血管被绷得过紧的医学意象，很容易转到被绷得过紧的神经上。

senses.title: An overcharged atmosphere
senses.definition: an excessively tense or overwrought quality in a situation, a debate, or a public mood
senses.definitionCN: 局势、争论或公共情绪中过度紧张、一触即发的状态
senses.example: The hypertension of the final week before the vote made quiet compromise impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 投票前最后一周那种高度紧张的气氛，让平静的妥协变得不可能。
senses.why: Once tension becomes a shared mood, any public scene can be described as running at dangerously high pressure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「紧张」成为一种共同情绪，任何公共场面都可以被形容为在危险的高压下运行。

intro.en: Hypertension joins a Greek prefix to a Latin noun: hyper- means over, and tension comes from tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: hypertension 把希腊语前缀与拉丁语名词接在一起：hyper- 表示「超过」，tension 出自 tendere「拉紧」。

items.en: Greek hyper meant over, above, or beyond, and it became a productive prefix in scientific English.
items.cn: 希腊语 hyper 意为在上、超过，后来成为科技术语中能产的英语前缀。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch or pull tight, and its noun tensio named a stretching.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为拉紧、伸张，其名词 tensio 表示拉伸。

items.en: The noun passed through French into English, where tension first named physical stretching.
items.cn: 这个名词经由法语进入英语，tension 最初指物理上的拉伸。

items.en: English extended tension from a stretched rope to strained nerves and strained relations.
items.cn: 英语把 tension 从绷紧的绳索扩展到紧绷的神经与紧张的关系。

items.en: Hypertension was coined in the 1890s for blood pressure that stays abnormally high.
items.cn: hypertension 在十九世纪九十年代被造出来，指长期异常偏高的血压。

items.en: The cuff and the threshold turned hypertension into a measured diagnosis, split into essential and secondary forms.
items.cn: 血压袖带与诊断阈值使高血压成为可测量的诊断，并区分出原发性和继发性两类。

note.en: Hypotension, tension and hypertensive share the stretching root, while high blood pressure, stress and strain are the everyday neighbours.
note.cn: hypotension、tension 与 hypertensive 共享「拉紧」这个词根；high blood pressure、stress 与 strain 则是日常语义上的邻居。

entries.definitionCN: 血压异常偏低，与 hypertension 只差一个前缀。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched tight, or mental strain
entries.definitionCN: 被拉紧的状态，或精神上的紧张；是 hypertension 的后半部分。

entries.definition: relating to high blood pressure, or a person who has it
entries.definitionCN: 与高血压有关的，或指高血压患者。

entries.definition: the everyday name for the same condition
entries.definitionCN: 同一种病的日常说法，比 hypertension 更口语。

entries.definition: pressure or worry caused by a difficult situation
entries.definitionCN: 困境带来的压力或忧虑，对应 hypertension 的引申义。

entries.definition: severe pressure or effort on the body or the mind
entries.definitionCN: 身体或精神承受的沉重压力，与「绷紧」的意象相通。

normalIntro.en: Hypertension is a Latin noun of stretching under a Greek prefix meaning over: pressure pulled past the line.
normalIntro.cn: hypertension 是希腊语「超过」加拉丁语「拉紧」：被拉过界线的压力。

normal.en: Hyper- means over, so hypertension is pressure over the normal line.
normal.cn: hyper- 表示「超过」，所以 hypertension 就是超过正常线的压力。

normal.en: Tension comes from Latin tendere, to stretch.
normal.cn: tension 出自拉丁语 tendere，意为拉紧。

normal.en: The adjective is hypertensive, and a hypertensive is also a person with the condition.
normal.cn: 形容词是 hypertensive，而 a hypertensive 也可以指高血压患者。

normal.en: Antihypertensive drugs push the pressure back down; hypo- is the opposite of hyper-.
normal.cn: antihypertensive 是降压药；hypo- 正是 hyper- 的反义前缀。

normal.en: A reading is written as two numbers, the upper systolic and the lower diastolic.
normal.cn: 血压写成两个数字：上面是收缩压，下面是舒张压。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber tube filled from inside until its wall turns pale and tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡胶管从里面被灌满，管壁发白、绷得紧紧的。

abstract.en: Imagine a gauge needle crossing the red line and staying there.
abstract.cn: 想象压力表的指针越过红线，就停在那里不再回落。

abstract.en: Think of a narrow pipe deep in the lungs taking the full push of the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象肺深处一根细管，独自承受心脏泵出的全部推力。

examples.en: Hypertension is often found during a routine check-up.
examples.cn: 高血压常常在常规体检中被发现。

examples.en: Untreated hypertension can damage the heart, the brain and the kidneys.
examples.cn: 未经治疗的高血压会损害心脏、大脑和肾脏。

examples.en: Pulmonary hypertension is not the same as the common form.
examples.cn: 肺动脉高压与常见的高血压不是一回事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨、怕、疼、身」——血压一高，头就发晕，别嗨、别怕、也别硬撑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hyper（在上、超过）＋拉丁语 tendere（拉紧）的名词 tensio（张力）→ 英语 tension → hypertension，字面即「张力过高」，十九世纪末起专指血压长期偏高。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a stretched artery, then names the high reading, a local pressure, and finally any tension pulled too tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从被绷紧的血管出发，继而指偏高的读数、局部高压，最后指任何被拉得过紧的紧张状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an artery stretched tight from the inside, the gauge needle in the red zone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从里面被撑紧的动脉，压力表指针停在红区。

branches.en: A long-term illness defined by pressure above the normal range.
branches.cn: 一种以压力长期高于正常范围来定义的慢性病。

branches.en: The single high reading that first reveals the illness.
branches.cn: 第一次暴露这个病的那个偏高读数。

branches.en: The same high pressure confined to the lungs or the liver.
branches.cn: 同样的高压被限制在肺部或肝部的循环里。

branches.en: Nerves or a public mood pulled as tight as an overfilled artery.
branches.cn: 神经或公共情绪被绷得像灌满的动脉一样紧。

branches.en: The disease and its number are two views of one measurement.
branches.cn: 疾病与其数值，是同一次测量的两个视角。

intro.en: Hypertension is built from the Greek prefix hyper- and the Latin noun tension, with hypertensive and antihypertensive as its main English relatives.
intro.cn: hypertension 由希腊语前缀 hyper- 与拉丁语名词 tension 构成，主要英语亲属是 hypertensive 与 antihypertensive。

latinIntro.en: Greek hyper means over or beyond; Latin tendere means to stretch, and tensio means a stretching.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hyper 意为在上、超过；拉丁语 tendere 意为拉紧，tensio 意为拉伸。

items.example: Tension keeps the Latin sense of stretching.
items.exampleCN: tension 保留了拉丁语「拉伸」的含义。

items.example: Tendere is the source of tension and tense.
items.exampleCN: tendere 是 tension 与 tense 的来源。

items.example: Tensio passed through French as tension.
items.exampleCN: tensio 经由法语成为 tension。
紧绷的肌肉一直处于拉伸状态。

items.meaningCN: 行为或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 血压正常的；血糖正常的

latinEntries.exampleCN: tendere 生出 tension 与 tense。

latinEntries.example: Tensio is the direct source of tension.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tensio 是 tension 的直接来源。
tensus 描述被拉紧的东西。

definition_zh: 糖尿病；多尿症；糖尿病的病情
definition_en: a chronic disease in which the body cannot control the sugar in the blood, or a related disorder that drains away too much water
core_image: 一根弯成虹吸的管子不停把水引走，管口旁落着一滴血
scene: 老人总口渴、夜里频繁起夜，检查后才知道是糖尿病。Years of thirst and nightly trips to the bathroom finally led to a diagnosis of diabetes.
sceneCN: 这里 diabetes 是「糖尿病」（第 1 个义项：身体无法控制血糖的慢性病）；句意为多年的口渴与夜间频繁起夜，最终被诊断为糖尿病。

collocations.zh: 带病生活；与糖尿病共存

derivatives.zh: 糖尿病的；也作名词指糖尿病患者
糖尿病前期，血糖已偏高但尚未达到糖尿病标准

senses.title: The sugar disease
senses.definition: a chronic disease in which the body cannot control blood sugar because insulin is missing or does not work
senses.definitionCN: 因胰岛素缺乏或失效，身体无法控制血糖的慢性病
senses.example: Diabetes can damage the eyes, the kidneys and the nerves when it is poorly controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 糖尿病控制不佳时，会损害眼睛、肾脏和神经。
senses.why: Greek diabetes named a siphon, because the illness seemed to draw fluid straight through the body and out.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 diabetes 本指虹吸管，因为这种病看上去把体液一路穿流排走。

senses.title: The condition as lived
senses.titleCN: 病情；被管理着的糖尿病
senses.definition: the ongoing condition in one person, especially as it is watched and controlled day by day
senses.definitionCN: 某个人身上持续存在、需要逐日监测与控制的病情
senses.example: Her diabetes is stable on two injections a day.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天注射两次，病情保持稳定。
senses.why: A diagnosis turns into a daily companion, so the word also names the managed state rather than the abstract disease.
senses.whyCN: 诊断会变成日常的伙伴，所以这个词也指被管理着的病情，而不只是抽象的疾病。

senses.title: Water diabetes
senses.definition: a rarer disorder in which the body cannot hold water and passes large amounts of dilute urine
senses.definitionCN: 一种较罕见的病症，身体留不住水，排出大量稀释的尿
senses.example: Diabetes insipidus is treated with a hormone that helps the kidneys keep water.
senses.exampleCN: 尿崩症用一种帮助肾脏保水的激素来治疗。
senses.why: The old name was given to any illness that drained the body like a siphon, and the water-losing form still carries it.
senses.whyCN: 旧名曾给任何像虹吸一样排空身体的病，这种失水的类型至今沿用这个名字。

senses.title: The two main types
senses.definition: either of the two main forms, type 1 and type 2, which differ in cause and in treatment
senses.definitionCN: 两种主要形式（1 型与 2 型）之一，成因与治法都不同
senses.example: Type 1 diabetes needs insulin from the start, while type 2 often begins with diet and tablets.
senses.exampleCN: 1 型糖尿病一开始就需要胰岛素，2 型则常从饮食和口服药开始。
senses.why: Once doctors split the disease by cause, the single word came to cover a small family of diagnoses.
senses.whyCN: 医生按病因把这种病分开之后，同一个词就覆盖了一个小小的诊断家族。

intro.en: Diabetes is Greek: dia- means through, bainein means to go, and the noun first named a siphon.
intro.cn: diabetes 来自希腊语：dia- 意为穿过，bainein 意为走，这个名词最初指虹吸管。

items.en: Bainein was the everyday verb for going or walking.
items.cn: bainein 是表示走、行走的日常动词。

items.en: Dia- through plus bainein go gave diabainein, to pass through.
items.cn: dia-（穿过）加 bainein（走）构成 diabainein，意为穿过。

items.en: Diabetes named a siphon, and Greek physicians used it for a disease that passed urine without stopping.
items.cn: diabetes 指虹吸管，希腊医生用它命名一种不停排尿的病。

items.en: Medical Latin kept the Greek word whole, and medieval translators handed it to European medicine.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语原样保留了希腊词，中世纪译者又把它交给欧洲医学。

items.en: English records diabetes in the sixteenth century as a name for excessive passing of urine.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪记录下 diabetes，用来指排尿过多的病症。

items.en: Mellitus, honey-sweet, was added for the sugar form, and insipidus, tasteless, for the water form.
items.cn: mellitus 意为「蜜甜的」，用来指糖尿型；insipidus 意为「无味的」，用来指尿崩型。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- prefix, while the near-meaning group names the sugar, the hormone and the related substances.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dia- 前缀；近义组则列出糖、激素与相关物质。

entries.definition: relating to diabetes, or a person who has it
entries.definitionCN: 与糖尿病有关的；也指糖尿病患者。

entries.definition: a drawing that explains how something works, sharing dia- but built on graphein, to write
entries.definitionCN: 说明运作方式的图；只共享 dia- 前缀，后半出自 graphein（写），词源不同。

entries.definition: a straight line across a circle, sharing dia- but built on metron, measure
entries.definitionCN: 穿过圆心的直线；只共享 dia- 前缀，后半出自 metron（测量），词源不同。

entries.definition: an abnormally high level of sugar in the blood
the hormone that moves sugar from the blood into the cells
entries.definitionCN: 把糖从血液送进细胞的激素。

entries.definition: the simple sugar that the blood carries as fuel
entries.definitionCN: 血液作为燃料携带的单糖。

normalIntro.en: Diabetes is dia- through plus betes going, the old name for a siphon that lets everything run straight out.
normalIntro.cn: diabetes 是 dia-（穿过）加 betes（走），旧名意为让一切直穿而出的虹吸管。

normal.en: Dia- means through, as it does in diameter and diagram.
normal.cn: dia- 表示穿过，diameter 与 diagram 也用它。

normal.en: Bainein is Greek for to go, so diabetes is what goes straight through.
normal.cn: bainein 是希腊语「走」，所以 diabetes 就是直穿而过的东西。

normal.en: Diabetic is both the adjective and the person who has the disease.
normal.cn: diabetic 既是形容词，也指糖尿病患者。

normal.en: Mellitus means honey-sweet, and insipidus means tasteless.
normal.cn: mellitus 意为蜜甜的，insipidus 意为无味的。

normal.en: Diabetes is uncountable: say that someone has diabetes, never a diabetes.
normal.cn: diabetes 不可数：说某人患糖尿病，不能说「一个糖尿病」。

abstract.en: Picture a bent siphon pulling water out of a jar and never stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯成虹吸的管子，不停把水从罐里引走，怎么也停不下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a small meter, a diary of readings and a pen on the kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房桌上放着一个小血糖仪、一本记录读数的日记和一支笔。

abstract.en: Think of a jug filled and emptied again and again through the night.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶在整夜里被一次次灌满，又一次次倒空。

examples.en: Diabetes is one of the leading causes of kidney failure.
examples.cn: 糖尿病是导致肾衰竭的主要原因之一。

examples.en: He was diagnosed with diabetes after a routine blood test.
examples.cn: 他在一次常规验血后被诊断出糖尿病。

examples.en: Gestational diabetes usually clears up after the baby is born.
examples.cn: 妊娠期糖尿病通常在孩子出生后消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呆啊，别吃糖」——读起来像在提醒控糖；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 dia-（穿过）＋bainein（走）→ diabainein（穿过）→ diabetes（虹吸管，转指多尿）→ 拉丁语病名 → 英语 diabetes；mellitus（蜜甜的）与 insipidus（无味的）是后来加在病名后的限定词。

sensesIntro.en: One image of fluid running straight through yields the sugar disease, the managed condition, the water form and the two clinical types.
sensesIntro.cn: 「液体直穿而过」这一个意象，生出糖尿病、被管理的病情、尿崩症与两种临床类型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a siphon that keeps drawing water out of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根不断把水从身体里引走的虹吸管。

branches.en: A disease that lets sugar build up in the blood.
branches.cn: 一种让糖在血液里堆积的病。

branches.en: The condition of one person, measured and managed each day.
branches.cn: 某个人逐日测量、逐日管理的病情。

branches.en: The water form that drains the body without touching sugar.
branches.cn: 只排水、不涉及糖的尿崩类型。

branches.en: A family of diagnoses split by cause and treatment.
branches.cn: 按病因与治法分开的一个诊断家族。

branches.en: Both forms keep the old siphon image of fluid passing straight through.
branches.cn: 两种类型都保留了「液体直穿而过」的旧虹吸意象。

intro.en: Diabetes is dia- plus betes, from bainein to go; mellitus and insipidus are Latin epithets added later.
intro.cn: diabetes 由 dia- 加 betes 构成，betes 出自 bainein（走）；mellitus 与 insipidus 是后来加上的拉丁语限定词。

latinIntro.en: Greek dia means through and bainein means to go; Latin mel means honey and insipidus means tasteless.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 dia 意为穿过，bainein 意为走；拉丁语 mel 意为蜜，insipidus 意为无味。

items.meaningCN: 表动作执行者或承受者的后缀

latinEntries.exampleCN: mel 生出 mellitus 与 mellifluous。

latinEntries.example: Mellitus was added to name the sweet urine.
latinEntries.exampleCN: mellitus 被加进病名，指尿甜。

latinEntries.example: Insipidus marks the form with dilute urine.
latinEntries.exampleCN: insipidus 标记出尿稀的那一型。

definition_zh: 哮喘；哮喘发作；喘息；心源性哮喘
definition_en: a chronic disease in which the airways narrow and breathing becomes difficult, or a bout of wheezing and breathlessness
core_image: 一根被从中间捏细的吸管，每次出气都带一声哨响
scene: 男孩在操场上跑了几步就停下，捂着胸口大口喘气。Cold air and running brought on his asthma within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 asthma 是「哮喘」（第 1 个义项：气道慢性炎症导致反复喘息的疾病）；句意为冷空气和奔跑在几分钟内就诱发了他的哮喘。

derivatives.zh: 哮喘的；患哮喘的；也作名词指哮喘患者
抗哮喘的；也作名词指平喘药

senses.title: The chronic airway disease
senses.definition: a long-term condition in which the airways are inflamed and narrow, so breathing is repeatedly difficult
senses.definitionCN: 气道长期发炎、变窄，导致呼吸反复困难的慢性病
senses.example: Her asthma is worse in cold weather and after exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 她的哮喘在冷天和运动之后会更严重。
senses.why: Greek asthma named panting, so the word began as the sound and effort of breathing rather than as damage to the lungs.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 asthma 本指喘息，所以这个词起初命名的是呼吸的声音与费力，而不是肺里的损伤。

senses.title: A bout of wheezing
senses.definition: a single bout of wheezing, coughing and tightness in the chest
senses.definitionCN: 一次发作，表现为哮鸣、咳嗽与胸口发紧
senses.example: The dust brought on an asthma attack within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘在几分钟内就引发了一次哮喘发作。
senses.why: The noun slides from the disease to the episode, because a patient feels the illness only when the airways close.
senses.whyCN: 名词会从疾病滑向一次发作，因为患者只有在气道收窄时才感到这个病。

senses.title: Cardiac asthma
senses.definition: wheezing and breathlessness caused by heart failure rather than by diseased airways
senses.definitionCN: 由心力衰竭而非气道病变引起的哮鸣与呼吸困难
senses.example: Cardiac asthma sounds like ordinary asthma but comes from a failing left heart.
senses.exampleCN: 心源性哮喘听起来像普通哮喘，实际源自左心衰竭。
senses.why: The same wheeze can come from a flooded lung, so doctors borrowed the name and added the heart.
senses.whyCN: 同样的哨音也可能来自被水淹的肺，于是医生借用了这个名字，再加一个「心」字。

senses.title: The old sense: panting
senses.definition: laboured or gasping breathing, the original sense that survives in medical descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 费力、急促的呼吸，这一本义仍留在医学描述中
senses.example: In older medical writing, asthma could mean any laboured breathing, not only the allergic disease.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的医学文献里，asthma 可以指任何费力的呼吸，并不限于过敏性哮喘。
senses.why: Before the disease was understood, the word named the visible struggle itself, and that older sense still colours medical use.
senses.whyCN: 在疾病被认识之前，这个词命名的是看得见的挣扎本身，这层旧义至今仍在医学用法里留下痕迹。

intro.en: Asthma comes straight from Greek, where it named panting and hard breathing before it named a disease.
intro.cn: asthma 直接来自希腊语，在成为病名之前，它先指喘息与费力的呼吸。

items.en: A reconstructed root for blowing or breathing is generally thought to lie behind the Greek words; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示「吹、呼吸」的原始印欧语词根藏在希腊词背后；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Azein meant to breathe hard or gasp, and it is probably related to anemos, wind.
items.cn: azein 意为费力呼吸、喘气，一般认为与 anemos（风）有关。

items.en: Asthma named panting or laboured breathing, and Hippocratic doctors used it for the symptom.
items.cn: asthma 指喘息或费力呼吸，希波克拉底学派的医生用它来描述症状。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek term, and it passed through medical Latin into the modern languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留了希腊词，它又经由医学拉丁语进入现代诸语言。

items.en: English records asthma in the fourteenth century, with the th that is now silent.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录下 asthma，拼写里保留着如今不发音的 th。

items.en: Doctors separated asthma from other wheezing diseases and redefined it as chronic airway inflammation.
items.cn: 医生把哮喘与其他喘鸣性疾病分开，重新把它定义为气道的慢性炎症。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that only share the opening sound, while the near-meaning group separates the symptom from neighbouring lung diseases.
note.cn: 形近组收集的只是开头音相近的词；近义组则把症状与邻近的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: affected by or relating to asthma
entries.definitionCN: 患哮喘的；与哮喘有关的。

entries.definition: a dangerous lack of oxygen in the body
entries.definitionCN: 身体严重缺氧；只是开头音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: the wasting away of a body part
entries.definitionCN: 身体某部位的萎缩；只是开头音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to breathe with a whistling sound
entries.definitionCN: 带着哨音呼吸，是哮喘发作最典型的表现。
较大气道的炎症，与哮喘的病变位置不同。

entries.definition: damage to the air sacs of the lungs
entries.definitionCN: 肺泡受损的疾病，常与吸烟有关，不是哮喘。

normalIntro.en: Asthma is a Greek word for panting, so it names the effort of breathing before it names the disease.
normalIntro.cn: asthma 是希腊语里表示「喘息」的词，所以它先命名呼吸的费力，再命名疾病。

normal.en: The th in asthma is silent, so the word sounds like az-muh.
normal.cn: asthma 里的 th 不发音，听起来像「阿兹玛」。

normal.en: Asthmatic is both the adjective and the person who has the disease.
normal.cn: asthmatic 既是形容词，也指哮喘患者。

normal.en: An asthma attack is one bout, not the whole disease.
normal.cn: an asthma attack 是一次发作，不是整个疾病。

normal.en: Asthma is uncountable, so it has no plural.
normal.cn: asthma 不可数，没有复数形式。

normal.en: Bronchitis and emphysema are different lung diseases, not types of asthma.
normal.cn: bronchitis 与 emphysema 是另外的肺部疾病，不是哮喘的类型。

abstract.en: Picture a runner bent over after a race, each breath a hoarse pant.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者赛后弯着腰，每一口气都是嘶哑的喘息。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pressed to the chest on a cold morning, every breath shorter than the last.
abstract.cn: 想象冷天早晨一只手按住胸口，每一口气都比上一口更短。

abstract.en: Think of a lung slowly filling with water while the heart labours to pump.
abstract.cn: 想象肺里慢慢积起水，而心脏还在吃力地泵血。

examples.en: Cold air can trigger asthma in many children.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能诱发许多儿童的哮喘。

examples.en: She has kept her asthma under control with an inhaler.
examples.cn: 她靠吸入器把哮喘控制住了。

examples.en: Cardiac asthma is treated by supporting the heart, not the airways.
examples.cn: 心源性哮喘的治疗重点是支持心脏，而不是气道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿兹玛」——呼气时那声「嘶」的哨音，就是 asthma，th 不发音；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 azein（费力呼吸）→ asthma（喘息）→ 拉丁语原样沿用 → 英语 asthma；一般认为与 anemos（风）同源，更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from a chronic narrow airway to a single attack, then to a wheeze borrowed by the heart and back to its oldest sense of hard breathing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从慢性变窄的气道走到一次发作，再走到心脏借用的哮鸣，最后回到「费力呼吸」这一最古老的含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an airway pinched like a straw, every breath ending in a whistle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根像吸管一样被捏细的气道，每次呼吸都以一声哨音收尾。

branches.en: A long-term narrowing that waits between attacks.
branches.cn: 一种在发作间隙潜伏的长期气道狭窄。

branches.en: One night of wheezing after dust or cold air.
branches.cn: 灰尘或冷空气之后的一夜哮鸣。

branches.en: A wheeze that comes from a flooded lung and a tired heart.
branches.cn: 来自积水肺与疲惫心脏的哮鸣。

branches.en: The old word for any hard breathing, before the disease had a name.
branches.cn: 在疾病有名字之前，对任何费力呼吸的旧称。

branches.en: The disease and its attacks are one narrow airway seen at rest and in crisis.
branches.cn: 疾病与发作是同一根狭窄气道在平静时与危机时的两种样子。

intro.en: Asthma is a Greek medical word; asthmatic adds -atic, and antiasthmatic adds anti-.
intro.cn: asthma 是希腊语医学词；加 -atic 得 asthmatic，加 anti- 得 antiasthmatic。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer supplies spirare, to breathe, and spiritus, breath; Greek bronchos names the windpipe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层提供 spirare（呼吸）与 spiritus（气息）；希腊语 bronchos 指气管。

latinEntries.exampleCN: spirare 生出 respire 与 inspire。
bronchus 生出 bronchial 与 bronchitis。
